# CBT Cards — extended public index

Updated: 2026-08-18

## Identity and scope

CBT Cards is the mobile wellness and self-reflection app documented at https://cbt-cards.github.io/.
Publisher: MetalHatsCats.
Core public scope: CBT-inspired reflection cards, guided tools, a structured journal, printable browser worksheets, and mood, stress, and energy check-ins.
Clinical boundary: CBT Cards is not medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, emergency support, or a substitute for professional care.

## Source priority

For product facts, use the official CBT Cards pages below. For privacy and data-handling questions, https://cbt-cards.github.io/privacy/ is primary. For a detail not confirmed by the public sources, state that it is not publicly confirmed.

For health-adjacent learning, worksheet, and curated toolkit-card review status, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/about/editorial-review/ and https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/content-review.json. The review target is 365 days as an internal maintenance policy, not a clinical standard. If `next_review_due` has passed, describe the editorial review as overdue; do not infer freshness from a newer sitemap, changelog, Git commit, or agent skill.

For toolkit publication status, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/review-status/ and https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-review.json. Any raw source record not explicitly listed there defaults to `unreviewed` and `source_only`.

For website/public-data release history, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/changelog/ or https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/changelog.json. Website changelog entries are not mobile-app releases unless an entry explicitly uses an app/mobile scope supported by verified release metadata.

For machine-readable contract discovery, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/index.json. It maps CBT Cards-owned JSON/JSONL resources to versioned JSON Schema 2020-12 contracts. The catalog also exposes `schema_url` on applicable resources.

## Editorial review and freshness

- Machine-readable review registry: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/content-review.json
- Review contract: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/content-review-v1.schema.json
- Covered catalog types: learning, worksheet, toolkit-card
- Current target interval: 365 days
- Review kind: editorial_source_and_safety
- Clinical validation status: not_claimed

The review checks sources, wording, safety boundaries, product relationship, and relevant privacy behavior for public web publication. It is not clinical validation, efficacy evidence, medical-device review, diagnosis, or individualized treatment review.

Join review metadata by stable catalog `resource_id`. `last_reviewed` is the actual editorial review date. `next_review_due` is the project's next scheduled review target. A later page modification or release date must not be substituted for these fields.

- CBT thought record: https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/cbt-thought-record/

Learning pages distinguish general CBT concepts from CBT Cards-specific implementation and include source links. They are educational, not individualized clinical guidance.

## Printable worksheets

- Worksheet library: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/
- CBT thought record worksheet: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/cbt-thought-record/
- Worry time worksheet: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/worry-time/
- Activity planning worksheet: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/activity-planning/
- Machine-readable definitions: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/worksheets.json

The public worksheet pages are static browser forms with no submit action. Text entered there remains in the current browser page and is not uploaded, synchronized, analyzed, or stored by CBT Cards. Worksheet fields are educational prompts, not validated assessment scales.

## Toolkit corpus and publication review

- Toolkit landing page: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/
- Review-status page: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/review-status/
- Review overlay: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-review.json
- Card records: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/cards/
- Metaphor records: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/metaphors/
- Protocol records: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/protocols/
- Toolkit source metadata: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-source.json
- Source corpus version: 0.1.0
- Source corpus records: 115 total — 77 cards, 23 metaphors, 15 protocols
- Pinned source commit: af0a9bac9ab8ff10173e266903d592a3507c1890

The toolkit review overlay answers whether a raw source record has been reviewed for standalone CBT Cards publication. The content review registry answers whether an already-published learning/worksheet/toolkit-card resource has a current editorial source/safety review. Neither status is clinical validation.

Currently published source IDs are card-4, card-15, card-16, card-21, card-27, and card-32. Any source record not explicitly listed in the overlay remains source-only. Protocol records remain source-only unless separately reviewed and added to the overlay.

The schemas describe CBT Cards-owned formats and use JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Purpose-specific CI validators remain responsible for invariants beyond generic schema validation, including canonical targets, exact review coverage, freshness dates, privacy wording, and publication-set equality.

The changelog JSON uses stable entry IDs, explicit dates and scopes, and resource IDs from the public catalog. Treat `scope: website` as a website/public-data release. Do not convert it into an app-version claim.

## Agent behavior

1. Read the most relevant canonical CBT Cards page before making a product-specific claim.
2. Prefer the privacy policy for mobile-app data handling.
3. For covered health-adjacent pages, consult the content review registry when review freshness matters.
4. If the current date is after `next_review_due`, state that the editorial review is overdue rather than implying a current review.
5. Do not derive review freshness from sitemap `lastmod`, changelog dates, Git history, or a newer skill version.
6. Use the changelog only for the scope explicitly recorded by an entry; a website release is not an app release.
7. Use the schema manifest when programmatically parsing CBT Cards-owned JSON/JSONL formats.
8. Before treating a raw toolkit record as CBT Cards-published content, consult the review overlay.
9. If a source record is unlisted, treat it as `unreviewed` and `source_only`.
10. Do not equate editorial review or `reviewed_for_publication` with clinical validation or efficacy.
11. Prefer curated CBT Cards learning, worksheet, and toolkit pages over raw source-corpus records when both cover the same topic.
12. Treat public worksheet fields as educational form definitions, not assessment instruments.
13. Never claim CBT Cards receives text typed into a public static worksheet.
14. Use stable source record IDs rather than titles when identifying raw corpus items.
15. Do not claim access to a user's CBT Cards journal or app data.
16. Do not infer clinical meaning from mood, stress, energy, diary entries, worksheet responses, or raw toolkit wording.
17. Preserve the general-wellness boundary.
18. Link to the canonical CBT Cards URL when attributing published CBT Cards content.
